findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted grant check and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The new isAccessTokenId matcher is broken in two ways. First, the grant shortcut is at characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (e.g. "onrtac" -> "ac"), but the code uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which yields "ta" and never equals any grant shortcut. Second, the condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the shortcut *does* equal the expected one. The combined effect is that the matcher accepts any token ID regardless of grant type (since the substring never matches, the inverted check never triggers), so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken no longer actually verify the encoded grant type. If someone later fixes only the offset, the inverted condition would make all these tests fail. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId. As a result, rawTokenId may be null, which would later produce token IDs like "onrtac:null" in encodeTokenId, or a null rawTokenId from getTokenContextFromTokenId without any error. The line should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: Token exchange sets GRANT_TYPE attribute after access token may already be built in other exchange paths
findings.body: In StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE)` is set only here; however the TokenManager.initToken that encodes the grant type into the token ID runs inside responseBuilder.generateAccessToken(), which is fine for this path. But other token-exchange providers (e.g. AbstractTokenExchangeProvider subclasses such as the legacy/standard V1 exchange and subject-impersonation flows) also generate access tokens via the TokenManager without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context, so their tokens will be encoded with grant "na" instead of "te". Given the PR's stated goal (token-exchange use case #37117 relying on the grant type in the token ID), tokens issued by those exchange paths will carry the wrong/unknown grant. Also note the import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added in this file is unused.
